tasks.title: Integrate Claude Code Router into Claude Gemini MCP Slim for Dynamic Model Routing and Multi-Provider Support
tasks.description: Incorporate the claude-code-router framework into the claude-gemini-mcp-slim project to enable intelligent, scenario-based model routing and multi-provider abstraction. Phase 1, focusing on core routing engine, scenario-based routing, and initial provider abstraction, is successfully completed, establishing a solid, extensible foundation. This integration is architecturally sound, aligns with industry best practices for extensible AI agent infrastructure, and preserves the existing MCP architecture and decoupled design principles.
tasks.details:
1. Analyze the claude-code-router repository to understand its architecture, focusing on model routing, multi-provider support, request/response transformation, and plugin systems as described in the official GitHub repository[1].
2. **Phase 1 Completion**: The core routing engine, including dynamic model selection, scenario-based routing (default, background, think, longContext, webSearch), token-aware routing, and cost-optimization routing, has been successfully integrated into `execution_orchestrator.py`, establishing the intelligent orchestration layer. Backward compatibility is preserved, with routing disabled by default.
3. **Phase 1 Completion**: The initial provider abstraction layer, including a base provider interface and Gemini provider implementation, has been established. This sets the stage for future multi-provider support (e.g., OpenRouter, DeepSeek, Ollama, Gemini, Volcengine, SiliconFlow).
4. **Phase 1 Completion**: Request and response transformers from claude-code-router have been integrated to customize interactions per provider, maintaining compatibility with existing Gemini API client enhancements (e.g., instructor library integration from Task 7).
5. **Phase 1 Completion**: The decoupled architecture has been preserved by implementing a middleware pattern for routing logic, enabling independent updates and testing, aligning with the CLAUDE.md module pattern.
6. **Phase 1 Completion**: Configuration options have been implemented to support scenario-based routing and enable/disable routing features, aligning with existing configuration management patterns (see Task 11).
7. Ensure robust error handling and logging for routing decisions and provider interactions, consistent with agentic workflow standards (see Task 12).
8. Document the integration approach, configuration options, and usage examples to facilitate developer adoption and maintenance.
9. Follow best practices for AI coding workflows and testing as outlined in Claude Code best practices and AI coding guides[3][4].
10. The overall three-phase approach (Enhanced Model Routing, Multi-Provider Support, Advanced Routing Logic) has successfully completed Phase 1 (Enhanced Model Routing), establishing a solid foundation for multi-provider capabilities and advanced routing strategies, maintaining the existing 'Intelligent Orchestrator' philosophy. Reference implementation: https://github.com/musistudio/claude-code-router
tasks.testStrategy:
- **Phase 1 Validation**: Configuration loading, middleware imports and initialization, and execution orchestrator integration have been validated. Legacy execution patterns are preserved and working. Code quality checks passed.
- Unit tests for core routing logic covering various scenarios (default, background, think, longContext, webSearch), token-aware, and cost-optimization routing.
- Integration tests validating end-to-end request routing through the initial Gemini provider within the MCP architecture.
- Mock tests simulating provider failures to verify fallback and error handling mechanisms.
- Performance tests to ensure routing does not introduce unacceptable latency.
- Configuration tests verifying correct application of routing preferences and toggles.
- Logging and error handling validation through simulated failure scenarios.
- Compatibility tests with existing agentic collaboration features and structured response handling (Tasks 7, 10, 12).
- Continuous integration pipeline validation to ensure stability across Python versions and environments (see Task 14).

subtasks.title: Phase 2: Multi-Provider Support
subtasks.description: Implement additional model provider integrations (e.g., OpenRouter, DeepSeek) leveraging the established provider abstraction layer and request/response transformation capabilities.
subtasks.details:
Building upon the Phase 1 foundation:
1. Create concrete provider implementations for OpenRouter and DeepSeek, following the established base provider interface and `claude-code-router` patterns.
2. Extend the existing transformer layer to handle specific request/response adaptations for OpenRouter and DeepSeek APIs.
3. Refine the provider-first, fallback-cascade architecture to seamlessly integrate new providers.
4. Implement provider-specific authentication and configuration management for OpenRouter and DeepSeek.
5. Enhance error handling and retry logic for multi-provider failures, ensuring robust fallback mechanisms.
6. Maintain existing security and input validation through `helpers/security.py` for all new provider interactions.

subtasks.title: Phase 3: Advanced Routing Logic
subtasks.description: Implement advanced routing strategies for performance optimization, cost efficiency, and enhanced telemetry, building on the multi-provider foundation.
subtasks.details:
Building upon the multi-provider support from Phase 2:
1. Enhance performance-based routing to dynamically select faster models for quick queries and more capable models for complex analysis.
2. Refine cost-optimization routing to intelligently select cheaper models for background tasks and premium models for critical operations, considering real-time cost data if available.
3. Deepen request context analysis to determine optimal routing strategy based on content type, size, complexity, and user preferences.
4. Implement comprehensive routing telemetry and analytics for real-time performance monitoring, cost tracking, and decision-making insights.
5. Add granular configuration options for routing strategy preferences (e.g., prioritizing cost, speed, or accuracy).
6. Ensure advanced routing logic seamlessly integrates while maintaining existing MCP architecture and orchestration patterns.
